thread:
jess: FYI customer (ACME) started seeing AccessDenied for KMS Decrypt after we did a cross-account alias swap. They're seeing 403s + latency spikes. Pasting minimal logs and a repro they ran. @andrew @priya :rotating_light:

jess: Command they ran:
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --encryption-context Project=acme --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:999888777:key/old-key-id
# -> AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111222333:assumed-role/app-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:999888777:key/new-key-id
```

andrew: Two quick checks: is this cross-account (acct 111222333 -> key in 999888777)? AccessDenied often means encryption-context mismatch or key policy/grant missing. If they swapped the alias to a new CMK and rewrapped ciphertext incorrectly the key-id in the blob could cause failure.

priya: Also check the key policy/implicit grants. If the key policy has a Condition on kms:EncryptionContext:Project (or exact map) any mismatch will deny. Can you paste the policy snippet?

jess: Customer says the rewrap script used the SDK without passing EncryptionContext (they thought context was optional). They encrypted some blobs with no context, then attempted decrypt with context and got 403. They also reported ~50k failed decrypt attempts in 2h -> billing spike.

andrew: Repro that locally quickly:
```bash
# encrypt with context
aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/rotation-test --plaintext "hi" --encryption-context Project=acme --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 --decode > ct1.bin
# decrypt WITHOUT context -> should fail
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct1.bin || true  # AccessDenied if context required
# encrypt WITHOUT context
aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/rotation-test --plaintext "hi" --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 --decode > ct2.bin
# decrypt WITH context -> fails
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct2.bin --encryption-context Project=acme || true
```

priya: Policy snippet we've seen before (example):
```json
{
  "Sid": "RequireProjectContext",
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "*"},
  "Action": "kms:Decrypt",
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {"StringNotEquals": {"kms:EncryptionContext:Project": "acme"}}
}
```
(They may have a similar allow/deny pattern.)

jess: CloudTrail sample they gave shows repeated kms:Decrypt errorCode=AccessDenied from same role. They're also throttling and retrying which pushed API bill up. They want an immediate mitigation.

andrew: Short-term mitigation options (pick one):
- Stop the clients/process that are auto-retrying (fastest).
- Roll back the alias to previous CMK if the old key still exists (alias -> old-key-id). That will immediately allow decrypts for ciphertexts still encrypted to the old key.
- Add a temporary policy exception to allow decrypts without the encryption-context for that principal (riskier).

priya: For a safe recovery I recommend: stop clients -> roll back alias -> run a controlled rewrap that ALWAYS includes the encryption-context, then update clients to include context, then swap alias forward. I'll draft a rewrap script.

jess: Customer asked for the exact check-list to confirm so their SRE can act. I'll pass your checklist. Any quick commands to query which key a ciphertext was encrypted with?

andrew: You can use AWS CLI to inspect ciphertext metadata: the first few bytes/header hold the key id but AWS won't decode locally. Best is to call kms:Decrypt and look at the error message AWS returns (it often includes key id mismatch). Otherwise, have them run `aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/whatever` to confirm alias targets. Also search CloudTrail for Encrypt events to see which key-id was used.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4321 (assigned to eng-security). Tags: kms, encrypt-context, cross-account, billing-impact.

andrew: I'll prepare a short playbook and a small rewrap script (with --encryption-context) and a policy diff example to post in the incident. :thumbsup:
